statcan_17100009.title: Population estimates, quarterly
statcan_17100009.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 17-10-0009-01 Population estimates, quarterly.
methodology_notes: Estimates are final intercensal from July 1, 1971 to April 1, 2021; final postcensal July 1, 2021 to July 1, 2023; updated postcensal Oct 1, 2023 to Apr 1, 2026; preliminary postcensal from July 1, 2026 (StatCan table note 3).
Before July 1, 1971 estimates are unadjusted for census net undercoverage and rounded to the thousand. This platform starts population series at 1971-07-01 to avoid that methodological break.

Northwest Territories and Nunavut are presented separately from July 1, 1991, on current boundaries, although Nunavut was legally created April 1, 1999 (table notes 4 and 5). Before July 1991 only the combined figure exists; the map shows the two territories as one combined region for those dates.
Quarterly estimates reflect components of change from the preceding quarter (table note 2).
limitations: Estimates are revised as new census and component data arrive; preliminary values may change.

naturalearth_admin1.title: Admin 1 – States, Provinces (1:10m), plus lakes, countries, rivers (1:50m)
limitations: Generalized cartographic boundaries (1:10m), current boundaries only. Suitable for national and provincial display, not for analysis or municipal scale. StatCan cartographic boundary files will replace these when municipal layers are added.

statcan_17100008.title: Estimates of the components of demographic growth, annual
statcan_17100008.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 17-10-0008-01 Estimates of the components of demographic growth, annual.
methodology_notes: NT and NU are separate from 1991/1992; before that only the combined figure exists (notes 2–3).
Births and deaths final to 2023/2024, updated 2024/2025, preliminary 2025/2026; other components have their own final/preliminary cut-offs (notes 4–14).

Net emigration = emigrants − returning emigrants; 1991 to June 2016 it also includes net temporary emigration. Emigration estimates were revised back to July 2016 with a different method (notes 21–22).
Non-permanent residents (work/study permit holders, asylum claimants and family) are StatCan estimates and differ from IRCC counts (notes 10, 19).
Residual deviation distributes the census error of closure across the intercensal period (note 12).
limitations: Components for the most recent years are preliminary and will be revised.

statcan_17100045.title: Estimates of interprovincial migrants by province or territory of origin and destination, quarterly
statcan_17100045.reporting_period: Quarterly, July 1971 to April 2026; summed here to July–June periods
statcan_17100045.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 17-10-0045-01 Estimates of interprovincial migrants by province or territory of origin and destination, quarterly.
methodology_notes: Data source changes: Family Allowance (July 1971–June 1976), CRA tax data (July 1976–June 2025), Canada child benefit data (from July 2025) (note 3).

Quarterly in- and out-migrant counts before 2011 are not fully comparable with later ones; summed quarterly gross flows can exceed annual counts because people who move more than once in a year are counted each time. Net migration is additive (note 9).
Before July 1991 only NT and NU combined are available; 1976–1991 totals exclude moves between NT and NU (notes 5–6).
Final to June 2025, updated July 2025 to March 2026, preliminary from April 2026 (note 7).
limitations: Gross flows are sums of quarterly moves (a 'moves recorded' measure), not unique people per year.

statcan_98100001.title: Population and dwelling counts: Canada, provinces and territories (2021 Census)
statcan_98100001.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 98-10-0001-01 Population and dwelling counts.
methodology_notes: Density here = quarterly population estimate ÷ 2021 Census land area. Land area is held constant across years (a derived measure).
limitations: Land area changes little but is not constant across censuses; densities for early years use 2021 area.

parlinfo_elected.title: Elections and Elected Candidates (ParlInfo web service)
parlinfo_elected.licence: Library of Parliament terms of use; attribution required
parlinfo_elected.attribution: Source: Library of Parliament, ParlInfo, Elections and Elected Candidates.
methodology_notes: Seats = count of candidates recorded as elected in each general election, by province and party, on election night (later floor crossings and by-elections are not reflected).
ParlInfo records 341 elected candidates for 2025-04-28 against 343 seats; the difference is shown, not filled.
limitations: Seats are not votes; popular vote shares are a separate dataset (Elections Canada) still to be added.

elections_canada_ovr45.title: Official Voting Results, 45th general election (2025), Table 11: voting results by electoral district
elections_canada_ovr45.licence: Elections Canada terms of use; reproduction permitted with attribution
elections_canada_ovr45.attribution: Two 2025 members reconciled against Elections Canada, Official Voting Results.
limitations: Used only to add the two members missing from the Library of Parliament file for 2025 (registry/reconciliations/parlinfo_2025_missing_members.json). No file is stored; the two rows were read from the published table.

parlinfo_prime_ministers.title: Prime Ministers of Canada
parlinfo_prime_ministers.licence: Library of Parliament terms of use; attribution required
parlinfo_prime_ministers.attribution: Source: Library of Parliament, ParlInfo, Prime Ministers of Canada.
methodology_notes: Transcribed from the ParlInfo table on 2026-11-11 (no machine-readable export found); the file is kept as the raw record.
limitations: Provincial premiers are not in ParlInfo; they need provincial legislature sources (planned).

statcan_34100126.title: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, housing starts, under construction and completions, all areas, annual
statcan_34100126.publisher: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC), via Statistics Canada
statcan_34100126.licence: CMHC Licence Agreement for the Use of Data (reuse permitted with accurate reproduction and clear acknowledgement; must not imply CMHC endorsement)
statcan_34100126.attribution: Source: CMHC, Starts and Completions Survey, via Statistics Canada Table 34-10-0126-01.
methodology_notes: Starts and Completions Survey: a start is the pouring of the footing; a completion is when 90% or more of the work is done (CMHC definitions).
'All areas' combines centres of 10,000+ (enumerated monthly) with smaller areas (estimated quarterly by sample).
Geographical areas are modified every 5 years to reflect census definitions, so data are not strictly comparable historically (table note).
limitations: Completions are new units only. They are not net additions to the housing stock: demolitions, conversions and units lost are not subtracted.
No territorial data in this table.
statcan_34100126.coverage: Canada and 10 provinces. No territories in this table.

statcan_17100159.title: Estimates of the number of private households by size on July 1st
statcan_17100159.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 17-10-0159-01 Estimates of the number of private households by size on July 1st.
methodology_notes: Final intercensal 2006–2020, final postcensal 2021, updated postcensal 2022–2024, preliminary postcensal 2025 (table note).
Derived from T1 Family File tax data, census data, census net undercoverage and population estimates.
limitations: Begins in 2006; no comparable annual household series for earlier years in this table.
Private households only; people in collective dwellings are excluded.

statcan_34100127.title: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, vacancy rates, apartment structures of six units and over, privately initiated in census metropolitan areas
statcan_34100127.publisher: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC), via Statistics Canada
statcan_34100127.licence: CMHC Licence Agreement for the Use of Data
statcan_34100127.attribution: Source: CMHC, Rental Market Survey, via Statistics Canada Table 34-10-0127-01.
methodology_notes: Privately initiated apartment structures of six units and over. Excludes condominiums rented out, secondary suites and other secondary rentals.
CMA boundaries follow the census and change every 5 years (table note).
limitations: City-level only: there is no provincial vacancy rate in this table. The map shows each CMA as a point at its core city.
statcan_34100127.coverage: 36 census metropolitan areas plus a CMA average; coverage of each CMA starts in different years

statcan_34100133.title: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, average rents for areas with a population of 10,000 and over
statcan_34100133.publisher: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC), via Statistics Canada
statcan_34100133.licence: CMHC Licence Agreement for the Use of Data
statcan_34100133.attribution: Source: CMHC, Rental Market Survey, via Statistics Canada Table 34-10-0133-01.
methodology_notes: This platform uses two-bedroom units in row and apartment structures of three units and over.
Average rent for all surveyed units (sitting tenants and new tenants), not asking rents for vacant units.
Status F = too unreliable to be published; '..' = not available. Both are left blank, never filled.
limitations: Current (nominal) dollars, not adjusted for inflation.
Average of the existing purpose-built rental stock; movers typically face higher rents than the average.

statcan_18100005.title: Consumer Price Index, annual average, not seasonally adjusted
statcan_18100005.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 18-10-0005-01 Consumer Price Index, annual average, not seasonally adjusted.
methodology_notes: The CPI is a fixed-basket price index, not a cost-of-living index (table note).
The rent index measures rent paid by all tenants (new leases, renewals, mid-lease), not asking rents for vacant units.
January 2019: the rent index moved from a matched-model to a hedonic method using Labour Force Survey rents (Prices Analytical Series 62F0014M2019002). Comparisons across 2019 mix methods.
limitations: An index shows change from its base, not a level: provinces cannot be compared on rent levels using the CPI.
statcan_18100005.coverage: Canada (rent from 1949), provinces from 1979; territories only as cities (Whitehorse, Yellowknife, Iqaluit)

statcan_11100190.title: Market income, government transfers, total income, income tax and after-tax income by economic family type
statcan_11100190.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 11-10-0190-01 Market income, government transfers, total income, income tax and after-tax income by economic family type.
methodology_notes: This platform uses median after-tax income of economic families and persons not in an economic family, in 2024 constant dollars.
Survey of Consumer Finances 1976–1992, Survey of Labour and Income Dynamics 1993–2011, Canadian Income Survey 2012 onward (series breaks).
limitations: Covers all family units, owners and renters together; it is not renter income, so it cannot be divided into rents to make a renter affordability ratio.
statcan_11100190.coverage: Canada and provinces from 1976; Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut from 2018 only

naturalearth_places.title: Populated places, simple (1:10m)
limitations: Used only to place census metropolitan areas on the map at their core city. Brantford, Guelph and St. Catharines–Niagara are not in this file and are listed, not mapped.

naturalearth_sr50m.title: Shaded Relief Basic (1:50m), version 2.0.0
naturalearth_sr50m.attribution: Shaded relief: Natural Earth (public domain), derived from SRTM Plus elevation.
limitations: Physical-geography context only. The relief does not represent any statistic shown on the map.
A cartographic hillshade generalised for 1:50m; Natural Earth embossed small islands by hand. Not suitable for measuring elevation.

Resampled to a 3 km grid in the map projection and clipped to the province outlines (pipeline/build_relief.py). Resampling adds no detail: the source cell is 2 arc-minutes (about 3.7 km north–south and roughly 1.3–2.4 km east–west across Canada), and it was itself downsampled and generalised by Natural Earth.
naturalearth_sr50m.coverage: World land areas; 10,800 x 5,400 pixels (2 arc-minutes, about 3.7 km at the equator). Canada is fully covered.

statcan_17100005.title: Population estimates on July 1, by age and gender
statcan_17100005.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 17-10-0005-01 Population estimates on July 1, by age and gender.
limitations: Annual estimates, not census counts. Final intercensal to 2020; postcensal from 2021 (to be revised after the 2026 Census); 2026 is preliminary.
Shares by age are calculated here from the published counts (age group divided by all ages).
Median age is taken as published; it is not recalculated.
statcan_17100005.coverage: Canada, provinces and territories. Northwest Territories and Nunavut separately from 1991; combined before

statcan_17100148.title: Population estimates, July 1, by census metropolitan area and census agglomeration, 2021 boundaries
statcan_17100148.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 17-10-0148-01 Population estimates, July 1, by census metropolitan area and census agglomeration, 2021 boundaries.
limitations: A census metropolitan area is a core of at least 50,000 people plus surrounding municipalities, 100,000 or more in total. It includes suburbs and some rural land, so it is not the same as 'urban'.
Today's (2021) boundaries are applied to every year back to 2001, so growth here is growth inside a fixed area, not the spread of the area.
Released in January 2026, before the latest provincial estimates, so its provincial totals differ slightly from table 17-10-0009-01. Shares are calculated within this table only.
Final intercensal to 2020; postcensal from 2021; 2025 is preliminary. Starts in 2001.
statcan_17100148.coverage: 41 census metropolitan areas and all census agglomerations, on 2021 boundaries for every year. Prince Edward Island and the three territories have no census metropolitan area

statcan_17100118.title: Selected population characteristics, Canada, provinces and territories
statcan_17100118.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 17-10-0118-01 Selected population characteristics, Canada, provinces and territories.
limitations: Census counts for eight census years; the series ends in 2006 and is not extended. From 2011 Statistics Canada replaced 'urban area' with 'population centre'.
Urban area: a continuously built-up area of 1,000 or more people at 400 or more per square kilometre, based on the previous census. Small towns count as urban.
Not comparable with the census-metropolitan-area share (table 17-10-0148-01), which uses a different definition.
statcan_17100118.coverage: Canada, provinces and territories. Northwest Territories and Nunavut combined to 1996, separate for 2001 and 2006

statcan_39100048.title: Population in core housing need by selected sociocultural characteristics, economic family structure and gender
statcan_39100048.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada. Table 39-10-0048-01. Census of Population 2016 and 2021.
methodology_notes: Core housing need: a household's dwelling falls below at least one of the adequacy (no major repairs), affordability (shelter costs under 30% of before-tax income) or suitability (enough bedrooms) standards, and it would have to spend 30% or more of before-tax income to rent acceptable local housing at the median rent (Census definition).

Only private, non-farm, non-reserve households with income above zero and shelter-cost-to-income ratios under 100% are examined. Non-family student households with a maintainer aged 15 to 29 are counted as not in need.
Counts are randomly rounded; percentages are computed by Statistics Canada.
This table counts persons living in households in core housing need, not households.
limitations: Census years only: no annual values exist between censuses, and none are estimated here.

2021 Census income refers to 2020, when temporary pandemic income supports lowered the share of income spent on housing; Statistics Canada attributes much of the 2016→2021 decline to these supports (The Daily, 2023-01-23).
On-reserve households are not examined, which matters most where many people live on reserve.
2011 values come from the voluntary National Household Survey and are not shown.
statcan_39100048.units: Percent of persons in private households examined for core housing need
statcan_39100048.coverage: Canada, provinces and territories. This platform shows 2016 and 2021 only.
